name: Content and channel strategy
shortDescription: Content strategy and channel planning for cardiology and MedTech brands: audience insight and segmentation, marketing strategy and content plans that put the right message in front of physicians, cath lab teams and buyers, on the channels they actually use.
whyThisMatters:
Content strategy decides what content a medical device or healthcare brand should make, for whom and where it will be used, so every production earns its place.

Most medical content is made one project at a time: a film for a launch, an animation for a congress. A content strategy joins it up. It starts with what your audience actually needs, organises it into pillars and formats, and plans how one shoot becomes a full film, short chapters, social versions and training modules on the channels your audience uses.

We research before we plan: calls with patients, clinicians and your teams, and a clear view of how physicians, staff and buyers find and use content. For a UK hospital group we turned that research into a patient-education film with thirteen short standalone chapters, and planned a series of fourteen short films across thirteen sites, each versioned for the platforms it would run on.

faqs.question: What is a content strategy for a medical device company?
faqs.answer: It is a plan for what content to make, for which audiences and where it will be used, so films, animations and campaigns work together over time rather than as one-off projects.

faqs.question: How do you research what an audience needs?
faqs.answer: We talk to them. For patient education that has meant informal calls with patients about what information mattered most to them, then working with clinical staff on the script.

faqs.question: Can one production give us content for several channels?
faqs.answer: Yes. We plan for it from the start: one full film, standalone chapters, social cuts in 9:16 and 1:1, platform versions and stills, all from the same shoot.

faqs.question: Does content strategy include channel planning?
faqs.answer: Yes. We plan where each piece will live, from YouTube playlists that play chapters in sequence to LinkedIn, congress screens and sales tools, and how it will reach the right people.
